subject: Genetics
title: Punnett Squares
description: A micro-lesson that makes Punnett Squares usable.

hook.text: A Punnett square is a simple grid that predicts offspring traits. Two alleles across, two down, four combinations.

buildup.text: Reginald Punnett invented it in 1905. It made Mendel's ratios visual and easy to calculate for anyone.

discovery.text: Cross Bb × Bb: you get BB, Bb, Bb, bb. Three show the dominant trait. One shows recessive. The 3:1 ratio appears.

twist.text: Punnett squares work for simple traits but fail for complex ones. Height involves hundreds of genes. No grid fits that.

climax.text: For single-gene traits like cystic fibrosis carrier status, a Punnett square predicts risk perfectly.

punchline.text: A 2×2 grid that predicts the next generation.

quiz.question: What does a Punnett square predict?
